chief_complaint: Fever, retro-orbital headache, jaundice, coffee-ground vomiting, gross haematuria, and increasing mental obtundation.
history_of_present_illness: Eight days prior, he developed fever and retro-orbital headache, followed two days later by jaundice, coffee-ground vomiting, gross haematuria, and increasing mental obtundation, leading to admission to a local jungle hospital; during transfer to Lima, he had a generalized seizure. His past medical history included hepatitis of unknown aetiology 20 years before.
exposure_and_epidemiology: The patient was born in Lima but for the past 5 years has worked as a logging supervisor in a remote jungle area near Pucallpa on the shores of the Ucayali River; he has not taken malaria prophylaxis and has not received any vaccinations since early childhood.
vitals: Temperature 38.8°C (101.8°C), blood pressure 110/70 mmHg, heart rate 110 beats per minute, respiratory rate 24 breaths per minute.
physical_exam: Patient was agitated, unresponsive to verbal commands, intermittently stuporous with marked flapping of hands, no focal neurological signs, no meningeal signs. He was jaundiced with spontaneous bleeding of oral mucosa, venipuncture, and IV sites, and had multiple large ecchymoses on the face, trunk, and all limbs. Lung auscultation revealed crepitant rales in both bases. Heart sounds were normal. Liver was palpable 3 cm below the right costal margin; spleen and lymphadenopathy were not palpable.
labs_and_diagnostics: Routine laboratory results on admission are shown in Table 93.1. Malaria thick film was three times negative, blood cultures were negative, Brucella serology was negative, and Hepatitis B IgM anti-Hbc were negative.
differential_diagnosis: Acute febrile illness with liver failure, severe malaria, viral hepatitis (A, B, C, D, E), toxin-mediated hepatitis, leptospirosis, typhoid fever, brucellosis, severe dengue, and other viral haemorrhagic fevers (VHFs) with jaundice, including yellow fever.
management_and_clinical_course: The patient received presumptive treatment for malaria, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and supportive care. Over the next 3 days, he developed increasing hepatic encephalopathy, renal failure, coma, and DIC with increasing spontaneous bleeding. A chest x-ray showed bilateral pulmonary infiltrates compatible with ARDS. Repeat laboratory results on day 3 showed deteriorated kidney function (creatinine 6.5 mg/dL, urea 120 mg/dL) and a sudden drop in liver transaminases (AST 100 U/L, ALT 200 U/L), indicating acute hepatic disintegration. The patient passed away 1 day later.
final_diagnosis: Yellow Fever, confirmed by IgM capture ELISA highly positive at 1:10000.
